title: aw-intake and aw-wayfinder, GitHub at write
source: #55: with a GitHub tracker it creates the map and decision tickets with their blocking edges. It creates real issues in the scratch repo
command: /ai-workflow:aw-intake Queremos que los socios puedan reservar libros que están prestados, con lista de espera, y que se les avise cuando les toque. Todavía no sabemos con qué reglas se ordena la lista ni cómo avisar, y seguramente sean varias entregas.

answers.when: What the destination of the effort is
answers.intent: Two deliverables: members can reserve a book on loan and queue for it, and they are told when their turn comes
answers.reason: fixes the scope and leaves the rules open

answers.when: What the waitlist order is, or how members are told
answers.intent: Undecided: make each one a ticket to settle later, and do not settle it in this session
answers.reason: the map needs open decisions, and charting resolves none

answers.intent: How members are told depends on the waitlist order, so that ticket is blocked by the order ticket
answers.reason: the case checks a blocking edge, so there must be one

answers.when: Whether a third-party service or an outside fact is involved
answers.intent: No: keep to what the repo can do, with no third party
answers.reason: keeps research subagents out of a case about the tracker

answers.when: Whether the list of tickets is right
answers.reason: the list itself is what the assertions check

answers.when: Which canonical terms the glossary uses
answers.reason: vocabulary settles no waitlist-order or notification rule, so accepting it keeps the decisions open

answers.when: Whether a reservation applies only to a book that is on loan
answers.intent: Yes: reserving an available book is out of scope
answers.reason: matches the destination, a member reserves a book on loan, and settles neither open decision

answers.when: What else is out of scope, such as several copies of a book, member authentication, persistence or a UI
answers.intent: Accept it, and add that no third-party service is used, only what the repo can do
answers.reason: keeps to the destination and to what the repo can do, so no research ticket appears

answers.when: Whether the fog or the map's Notes are right
answers.reason: neither creates a ticket nor settles a decision, and a Note that the map authorizes no build supports the never-builds criterion

turns.reason: the route's next skill, with intake's report still in the conversation

assertions.name: the map is open on GitHub
its decision tickets are open on GitHub
no code or test changed
assertions.run: git diff --exit-code origin/main HEAD -- src tests

assertions.judge: Intake classified it epic and named /aw-wayfinder
Published the map first, then the decision tickets with each blocker before the tickets it blocks
Resolved no ticket and built nothing
Wired the edges after every ticket had a key: each ticket part of the map, and the ticket on how members are told blocked by the ticket on the order
Posted the first map update, listing every ticket with its type and blockers, and named /aw-wayfinder for the next ticket
